Ravindra Singh vs Samsung India Electronics Ltd. & Anr. on 8 August, 2023

 RAVINDRA SINGH VS SAMSUNG INDIA ELECTRONICS LIMITED AND ORS

 IN THE DELHI STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES
 REDRESSAL COMMISSION

 Date of Institution: 22.09.2014

 3. ADITYA INFOCOM
 BUILDING NO.14, BASEMENT CENTRAL MARKET
 NEAR HANUMAN MANDIR, ASHOK VIHAR PHASE 1

 ( Through: Mr. Lakshay Agarwal, Advocate)
 For Respondents No.1 & 3

 ALLOWED PAGE 1 OF 10
 FA/938/2014 DOD.:08.08.2023
 RAVINDRA SINGH VS SAMSUNG INDIA ELECTRONICS LIMITED AND ORS

 CORAM:
 HON'BLE JUSTICE SANGITA DHINGRA SEHGAL
 (PRESIDENT)
 HON'BLE MS. PINKI, MEMBER (JUDICIAL)
 HON'BLE MR. J.P.AGRAWAL, MEMBER (GENERAL)

 Present: Mr. Yashpal Singh, Counsel for the Appellant.
 Mr. Lakshay Agarwal, Counsel for the Respondent
 No.1&3
 None for the Respondent no.2.

 PER: HON'BLE JUSTICE SANGITA DHINGRA SEHGAL,
 PRESIDENT
 JUDGMENT
1. The facts of the case as per the District Commission record are:
"The complainant had purchased a Samsung Galaxy
 SGI-9003 mobile from OP No.2 for a total sum of
 Rs.17,900/-. The mobile phone was warranteed for a
 period of one year from the date of its purchase i.e.
 05.10.2011. It is alleged by the complainant that on
 30.10.2012 while the mobile handset was still under
 warranty, its touch function had stopped working. He had
 taken the mobile handset to the authorized service centre,
 OP No.3 and was informed that the mother-board of the
 handset was faulty. It was also informed to him that the
 particular part was not covered under warranty and he
 had to 12 pay for the replacement of the part. The
 complainant had protested and had told the OP No.3 that
 since the handset was under warranty, it should be
 repaired free of cost. OP No.3 further did not agree and
 charged a sum of Rs.7,780/- for replacement of the
 handset. It is alleged by the complainant that the mother
 board did not need to be replaced which is clear from the
 fact that the old mother-board was not handed over to
 him by OP No.3 after the repairs of the handset. He has,

 ALLOWED PAGE 2 OF 10
 FA/938/2014 DOD.:08.08.2023
 RAVINDRA SINGH VS SAMSUNG INDIA ELECTRONICS LIMITED AND ORS

 therefore, approached this forum for redressal of his
 grievance. "
2. The District Commission after taking into consideration the
 material available on record passed the judgment dated
 21.04.2014, whereby it held as under:
"We have heard arguments advanced at the bar and have
 perused the record. On behalf of the OPs, an affidavit has
 been filed by Sh. Suresh Kumar, an Authorized Representative
 of the OPs. Para 7 of his affidavit is relevant for the purpose
 of decision of this complaint and is being reproduced as under
:-
"7. I say that the complainant some problem had arisen in the
 said product and it is further rectified to the satisfaction of
 complainant. It is submitted that the complainant has
 purchased a phone from the Opposite Party No.2. In a good
 condition but due to mishandling of the phone by the
 complainant, some problem but due to mishandling of the
 phone by the complainant, some problem arose which was
 totally due to the fault of the complainant. It is further
 submitted that the complainant issue was duly resolved with
 and was assured of some solution. It is further submitted that
 OP NO.1 and 3 are still ready to resolve the issues with the as
 per the terms and conditions of the warranty policy. It is
 submitted that each time the complainant got the mobile
 respondent always entertained his complaint and solved it
 each time the complainant came and repair charges cannot be
 paid back because there was physical damage due to
 complainant's mistake."
In view of the affidavit filed by Sh. Suresh Kumar, we are
 unable to hold that the mother-board of the handset was
 under warranty and was required to be replaced free of cost.
 Rather we hold that there was no deficiency in service on the
 part of the OPs in charging a sum of Rs.7,780/- for
 replacement of the mother-board. Consequently, we hold that

 ALLOWED PAGE 3 OF 10
 FA/938/2014 DOD.:08.08.2023
 RAVINDRA SINGH VS SAMSUNG INDIA ELECTRONICS LIMITED AND ORS

 the complaint has no merits and the same is hereby
 dismissed."
3. Aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment of the District Commission,
 the Appellant has preferred the present appeal submitting that the
 District Commission has passed the Impugned Order in total
 disregard of principles of natural justice by merely considering the
 affidavit in evidence filed by the Respondent and by not taking
 into consideration any other material filed before it. Secondly, it is
 submitted that the observation made by the District Commission
 that the mobile handset had broken down due to mishandling is
 wholly perverse since it was nobody's case before the District
 Commission that the handset was broken down, neither in the
 written statement nor in the evidence. It is further contended that
 the District Commission erred in holding that the motherboard of
 the mobile was not under warranty since there was no such
 submission or argument advanced by the Respondent/Opposite
 Party. Yet, the District Commission went on to not only consider
 the same but also made such assumption the very basis of the
 Impugned Order. Thirdly, it is submitted that the Respondent
 No.3 refused to give the change parts back to the Appellant. It is
 further submitted that no parts were changed since the phone had
 some minor fault in the touch panel which was repaired and the
 Appellant was duped since he was charged Rs.7780 for the
 motherboard which was never changed. Lastly, it is submitted that
 the fine print of the warranty slip cannot be read by the naked eye
 and is contained inside the sealed box which is revealed to the
 consumer only after he purchases the handset. Therefore, the

 ALLOWED PAGE 4 OF 10
 FA/938/2014 DOD.:08.08.2023
 RAVINDRA SINGH VS SAMSUNG INDIA ELECTRONICS LIMITED AND ORS

 warranty terms, whether acceptable to the consumer or not, are
 imposed on him unilaterally, which amounts to unfair trade
 practice. Pressing the aforesaid contentions, the Appellant has
 prayed that the Impugned Order be set aside.
4. The Respondents No.1 & 3 have filed their joint reply and have
 stated therein that the Respondent No.1 & 3 have not violated any
 terms and conditions of the warranty policy nor have they adopted
 any unfair trade practice. It is further submitted that there is neither
 any manufacturing defect in the mobile phone or any deficiency in
 the services provided by the Respondent No.1. Lastly, it is
 submitted that by way of the present Appeal, the Appellant is
 wrongfully traying to extract compensation from the Respondent
 No.1 without any deficiency in service on part of the Respondent
 No.1. Pressing the aforesaid contentions, the Respondents have
 prayed that the present Appeal be dismissed.
5. During the course of the proceedings, the Respondent No.2 was
 directed to file its reply. However, despite giving multiple
 opportunities, Respondent No.2 failed to file its reply and was
 proceeded ex-parte vide order dated 24.05.2017.
6. We have perused the Appeal, Reply of the Respondents, the
 District Commission record and the Impugned Judgment.
7. The only question that falls for our consideration is whether the
 District Commission erred in ascertaining that the motherboard
 was not covered under warranty and wrongly dismissed the
 Complaint of the Appellant/Complainant.
8. A perusal of Impugned Order reflects that the District Commission
 has based its observation that the mother board of the handset was

 ALLOWED PAGE 5 OF 10
 FA/938/2014 DOD.:08.08.2023
 RAVINDRA SINGH VS SAMSUNG INDIA ELECTRONICS LIMITED AND ORS

 not under warranty by solely relying on the affidavit filed by Mr.
 Suresh Kumar, Authorized Representative of the
 Respondents/Opposite Parties. To resolve this issue, we deem it
 appropriate to refer to the warranty conditions reproduced
 hereunder as:
ALLOWED PAGE 6 OF 10
 FA/938/2014 DOD.:08.08.2023
RAVINDRA SINGH VS SAMSUNG INDIA ELECTRONICS LIMITED AND ORS
9. A bare perusal of the aforesaid warranty conditions makes it clear
 that the warranty pertains to the entire product and the aforesaid
 conditions nowhere mention about warranty in regard to specific
 parts i.e. the motherboard in the present case. It is implausible as
 how an inference can be drawn that the motherboard is not covered
 under warranty when the warranty conditions nowhere make a
 mention that the motherboard is excluded from the terms of
 warranty.
ALLOWED PAGE 7 OF 10
 FA/938/2014 DOD.:08.08.2023
RAVINDRA SINGH VS SAMSUNG INDIA ELECTRONICS LIMITED AND ORS
10. Furthermore, it is not in dispute that the Appellant approached the
 Authorized Service Centre of Samsung i.e. Respondent No.3 for
 the first time on 30.07.2012 and reported an issue pertaining to the
 touchscreen. It is also not in dispute that the warranty of the said
 product was still subsisting when the issue pertaining to the
 touchscreen was reported to the Respondent No.1. Here, is to be
 noted that after due inspection of the phone by the technicians of
 the Respondent No.1, the Appellant was informed that the mother
 board was faulty/damaged. However, no cogent material has been
 placed on record to show that there was physical damage on
 account of manhandling the phone. Further, no reasons or detailed
 reply has been filed to show that the said fault/physical damage in
 the motherboard is attributable to the user on account of
 manhandling the phone and is not an inherent/manufacturing
 defect. Therefore, we opine that a mere submission that the phone
 was damaged devoid of any corroborative evidence cannot be the
 sole ground to raise an adverse inference against the Appellant.
11. Moreover, we deem it appropriate to reproduce the relevant terms
 and conditions as referred to by the Respondents in their reply
 hereunder :
ALLOWED PAGE 8 OF 10
 FA/938/2014 DOD.:08.08.2023
RAVINDRA SINGH VS SAMSUNG INDIA ELECTRONICS LIMITED AND ORS
12. The aforesaid terms and conditions clearly state that the company
 shall repair or replace free of charge any part or parts of the
 product, if the defect is due to the faulty material or workmanship.
 It is to be noted that in the present case the Appellant purchased
 the mobile phone 05.10.2011 and the issue in the mobile phone
 was brought to the notice of the Respondent No.3 for the first time
 on 30.07.2012 i.e within 9 months from the date of purchase. It is
 to be further noted that the Appellant has been charged Rs.7780/-
 for replacing the faulty motherboard when the product was still
 under warranty. Furthermore, the Respondent No.1&3 failed to
 provide the replaced/faulty part to the Appellant, thus a negative
 presumption can be raised against the Respondent No.1&3 as to
 the genuineness of the service rendered and indulgence in unfair
 trade practices.
13. However, it is pertinent to remark that in light of the material on
 record, no fault or deficiency in service can be attributed to the
 conduct of Respondent No.2. It is to be noted that Respondent
 No.2 only acted in the capacity of a dealer selling the mobile
 phone and had no role to play either in manufacturing or repairing
 the phone. Thus, we opine that the Respondent No.2 cannot be
 held liable for providing deficient services.
14. Therefore, in view of the aforesaid discussion, we are not in
 agreement with the view taken by the District Commission and set
 aside the order dated 21.04.2014 passed by the District Consumer
 Disputes Redressal Commission, North-West, Shalimar Bagh
 Delhi-110088. Consequently, the First Appeal No.938/2014
 stands allowed and the Respondents No.1 & 3 are directed to :
ALLOWED PAGE 9 OF 10
 FA/938/2014 DOD.:08.08.2023
RAVINDRA SINGH VS SAMSUNG INDIA ELECTRONICS LIMITED AND ORS

 A. Refund the sum of Rs.7780/- taken from the
 Complainant within one month from 08.08.2023 (being
 the date of the present judgment)
 B. Pay to the Complainant a sum of Rs. 50,000/- as cost for
 mental agony
 C. Litigation Cost to the extent of Rs.25,000/-
15. Being guided by the principles as discussed above, in case the
 Respondents fail to pay the entire amount as mentioned in para 14
 of this judgment on or before 08.09.2023 (i.e. within one month
 from the date of the present judgment), the entire amount is to be
 paid alongwith simple interest @ 6% p.a. calculated from
 08.08.2023 till the actual realization of the amount.
16. Application(s) pending, if any, stand disposed of in terms of the
 aforesaid judgment.
17. The judgment be uploaded forthwith on the website of the
 commission for the perusal of the parties.
18. File be consigned to record room along with a copy of this
 Judgment.
(JUSTICE SANGITA DHINGRA SEHGAL)
 PRESIDENT
